subject: journey/nearchus
prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: journey sketchbook card.
One landscape 3:2 page from a historical travel sketchbook. Loose visible graphite construction lines, quick sepia hatching, restrained uneven watercolour washes in ochre, grey-green and faded blue, irregular unfinished edges dissolving into lightly foxed cream paper. Observed and modest rather than cinematic or fantasy. One integrated scene, no border, no inset drawings, no legible text, labels, annotations or signature.
Date and region: 325 BCE, Patala.
Subject and composition: High oblique view across a broad ancient Indus delta tidal channel, sandbars and reeds, a small line of ancient wooden oared vessels following the water towards a hazy sea. Landscape occupies almost all the page; boats distant, no foreground figures, no map, no lettering, no modern concrete canals. Realistic connected river water, not ships on sand.
When vessels appear: fourth-century BCE wooden oared ships with one simple mast and square sail, or sail furled; coherent curved hull, evenly aligned oars attached at gunwales, steering oars rather than wheels. No lateen sails, Viking dragon heads, modern rigging, engines or modern harbour works.
Do not insert Alexander or a recurring admiral into this scene. Follow the stated framing: landscape and object pages must not become foreground portraits.
Maintain anatomically sound hands, bodies and animals, physically consistent boat-water relationships, plausible ancient materials. Respect the specific viewpoint and main subject.
